hypotheses.claim: The designed common RAMP slope itself is too steep
hypotheses.conclusion: REFUTED for the designed common RAMP (calculated); REFUTED for the recorded v(ramp)
hypotheses.evidence: Ideal k x RAMP tracking slope at the -10 % RAMP capacitance is at most 0.3137 V/ms (+5) and 0.7611 V/ms (-12); the recorded peaks are 1.938x-3.044x the ideal and lie inside the low-voltage exception regions only. The extracted v(ramp), scaled by the tracking gain between 2 us bin averages within +/-100 us of each excursion, peaks at 0.1192 V/ms (+5) and 0.3529 V/ms (-12) in run 43087070975 (REPRODUCED, d1-reference-20261111.json).

hypotheses.claim: A start-order clamp release (U15/U16 on RAMP_P5/RAMP_M12 behind RCP1 1k) presents a fast reference-side edge to the +5/-12 trackers
hypotheses.conclusion: REFUTED for a reference-side edge; REFUTED for clamp-diode release
hypotheses.evidence: Scaled per-rail reference peaks between 2 us bin averages are 0.1192 V/ms (+5, ideal 0.3137) and 0.3557 V/ms (-12, ideal 0.7611); the clamp diodes stay reverse-biased across each window (+5: -4.850 to -4.843 V; -12: -4.893 to -4.041 V). The excursions lie downstream of the reference; run 43087070975 (REPRODUCED, d1-reference-20261111.json).

hypotheses.claim: The adjacent-sample reference rule fired on a solver-timestep artefact, not a circuit edge
hypotheses.conclusion: +5: NOT APPLICABLE (the adjacent-sample rule did not fire); -12: SUPPORTED
hypotheses.evidence: The -12 adjacent-sample peak of 3730.2 V/ms is 0.977 mV over 2.11 ns, inside a 21-sample cluster (minimum step 0.235 ns) where ramp_m12 rings 1.398 mV peak to peak with 18 sign reversals as the XU16A clamp output reaches 4.962 V. The 2 us bin-average analysis no longer lets such a step fire the rule; the in-job adjacent-sample classification is retained as superseded.

hypotheses.claim: The excess is a maximum-step artefact
hypotheses.conclusion: REFUTED for maximum step; UNRESOLVED for other solver settings and macromodel accuracy
hypotheses.evidence: 5 us to 2 us changes the peak by +0.01034 % (+5) and +0.01040 % (-12); reltol/abstol/method and vendor-model fidelity were not varied for these cases.

hypotheses.claim: Slope and current exceedances are one constraint, not two
hypotheses.evidence: The recorded ESR-branch currents equal C x dV/dt at the peak within ESR effects (+5: 114.58 vs 114.51 mA; -12: 265.46 vs 265.26 mA), and each current ceiling corresponds to the slope ceiling at contract capacitance (114 mA / 120 uF = 0.95 V/ms against 0.95 V/ms (equal); 265 mA / 180 uF = 1.4722 V/ms against 1.47 V/ms (slope ceiling tighter)). For the modeled pure C + ESR load a correction must reduce the slope; a current-only argument cannot pass. A load with a resistive or nonlinear part would separate the two.

hypotheses.claim: No-load excursions come from the pair passing its pre-bias target near conduction onset with no load to pull the output back
hypotheses.evidence: Consistent with no-load-only occurrence and the low-voltage location, and with the phase-10 prose. Distinguishing it needs one paired run changing only the pre-bias target (RT12O/RT5O/RT12NO) or integrator CT on nom/adv, after design review. Not run.

hypotheses.claim: The servo driver is wound up at a supply during the dead zone and its recovery sets the peak
hypotheses.conclusion: windup SUPPORTED; peak coincides with recovery NO; dead zone set by CONDUCTION THRESHOLD AFTER WINDUP
hypotheses.evidence: Pre-registered servo criteria on 2 us bin means: +5: driver left its supply 11.942 ms before the pass pair conducted, Vgs -0.000 to 2.443 V, conduction 368 us before the failed segment; -12: driver left its supply 10.858 ms before the pass pair conducted, Vgs -0.515 to 2.352 V, conduction 604 us before the failed segment; run 43099431981 (REPRODUCED, d1-servo-20261111.json).
Small negative adjacent-sample increments remain; no numerical tolerance is adopted.

C2 minimum-load bleeder.reason: The CSD18543Q3A pair is both the servo pass device and the output disconnect, so no passive bleeder can keep it conducting at the floor without defeating disconnection or the AGND-returned discharge.

EN-gated opposite-rail current sink.reason: Needs the disconnect and AGND-return rules reinterpreted and adds an enable-edge reverse-excursion risk.

C1 gate pre-bias while enabled.reason: A fixed floor cannot fit the threshold window: one that leaves a 2.0 V gap on a 2.7 V part leaves about 0.8 V on a 1.5 V part (guaranteed VGS(th) 1.5-2.7 V at 25 C). On -12 V the enable transient already brings Vgs within 8.1-9.7 mV of the model onset. No evaluated -12 V gap passed and no +5 V gap was evaluated (d1-gap-attempt2-20261111.md); the microvolt rule 6 results are not the reason.

T1 reset-window integrator leak.status: REJECTED by construction (owner decision 2026-11-11; not evaluated in transient)
T1 reset-window integrator leak.reason: DC balance at the summing node sets the driver by offset currents, not by conduction: +5 V DRV = 1.214 V - 43.1 x out (stays wound to its rail); -12 V DRV = 23.5 x out + 1.214 V (a -0.47 V threshold-dependent pedestal). Changing R only rescales it.

T2 peak-hold anti-windup clamp.status: FAIL on -12 V, attempt 1 (rules 6, 9 and L2; not adopted); REJECTED by construction on +5 V

+5.status: REJECTED by construction (owner decision 2026-11-11; not evaluated in transient)
+5.reason: RG2P (100 kohm, P5_G to P5_CS) carries Vgs/100 kohm; with the pair off it leaves P5_CS only through Q4's body diode into P5_OUT, so a gate held near the edge injects 8-20 uA against the 1.6 uA divider drain: a threshold-dependent output pedestal.
+5.option_b: Candidate (RG2P returned to GND) passes its paper check; pre-registration HELD pending the deck-stiffness item (owner decision 2026-11-12). Not adopted.
+5.floor_finding: RG2P explains at most 4.6 mV (19 %) of the 24 mV excess of the 52 mV floor over 28 mV; the floor is left as it is.

-12.summary: Rule 1 passes on the D1 failure deck (1.064 V/ms, 0.1915 A). Rule 6 (135.4 uV) and loaded L2 (about 0.3 mV) fail on DT2C junction capacitance coupling the capture step into trk12n_fb; rule 9 fails by 26 nV on a deck-wide disable kick at vntol (identical in the inert control). The four corners, t2/nom, t2lo, t2hi and t2load/nomR ABORTED.

T2 peak-hold anti-windup clamp.gate_hold_constraint: Any future +5 V or +12 V gate-hold scheme must idle at Vgs <= about 0.16 V at no load (Vgs / 100 kohm <= 1.6 uA through RG2P or RG1P and the output-side body diode), unless the gate pull-down return is changed.
T2 peak-hold anti-windup clamp.d1: HELD: a -12 V only result does not close D1 until +5 V has an answer.

bias_current_low_side_margins.rule: The limiter shunts sit upstream of each pair, so bias or bleeder current is sensed: delivered current at trip becomes trip_max - I_bias (the maximum-delivered margin grows), while the transient-minimum and startup-into-full-load margins shrink by I_bias.

d1_enable_edge.status: RECORDED NEGATIVE (owner decision 2026-11-11; no order hold)
d1_enable_edge.question: Would a fitted part at typical 2.0 V or minimum 1.5 V VGS(th) conduct at the enable edge and produce an output excursion?
d1_enable_edge.finding: Inference from a single-threshold model: the enable transient is the designed pre-bias; the loop stops at the pair's own conduction edge, so the distance to onset moves by at most a few mV under a 0.5 V emulated threshold shift and the enable-window output stays at its floor (+5 at most 51.9 mV against the 0.8 V hold screen; -12 and +12 below the 1.5 V analog threshold).
d1_enable_edge.open_check: Constant-offset threshold corners on the unchanged decks, mapped from the model 250 uA point (2.163 V on the +5 ramp): +5 VO2 -0.66 V and +0.54 V; -12 VO3 -0.66 V and +0.54 V. Untested today: -12 below the model threshold and +5 beyond -0.5 V. Rides on the next dispatch.

assumptions: Ideal simultaneous disconnect at t = 0 (disconnect-before-discharge, AGND connected).
Discharge switch on-resistance omitted (it only lengthens decay).
Disconnect skew between the rails is taken as zero; the contract allows up to 1 ms and the installed skew is unbounded (see disconnect_order).
Loads are fixed resistors at the 20 ms transient minimum; the OSC load-versus-voltage characteristic is UNSOURCED.

'Absent' is not defined numerically by the contract; the cases use the rail discharge level (0.5 V) as a labelled assumption, add the contract's informal 'about 1.5 V', and the undefined case stays OPEN.
OSC +/-12 V loads are largely rail-to-rail, which couples the rails; one-rail-to-AGND loads are an illustrative assumption, not the OSC load.

disconnect_order.reason: Disconnect and discharge start from the same EN_E state with no designed ordering, through unequal paths: +12/+5 disconnect EN_E -> Q33 -> EN_N (REN 10k pull-up) -> Q10/Q11; -12 disconnect Q24 -> RG3A 56k -> Q25; discharge from the CDH hold-up: Q56 -> DIS_P (R60 100k pulldown) -> Q51/Q52, and Q54 -> R61 470k / R62 1M divider -> Q55. Relative timing needs device switching data and the CSD18543Q3A gate-charge path, which the decks omit. Overlap current is limited by the discharge resistors (above); that is a consequence, not compliance.

hypotheses.claim: At zero load the discharge resistors alone meet the level, time and voltage-form rows
hypotheses.conclusion: SUPPORTED only for absent <= 1.44 V with ideal simultaneous disconnect (calculated); disconnect order is D2-H3
hypotheses.evidence: All rails reach their discharge level inside 100 ms. With absent = 0.5 V there is no R-VEE, direct-hazard or screen event; R-VEE first fails at an absent threshold of 1.45 V, and at 1.5 V it fails (zero_load_absent_1_5v).

hypotheses.claim: Independent asymmetric loads can reorder decay into a forbidden state
hypotheses.conclusion: SUPPORTED under the stated resistive-load and absent-threshold assumptions; UNRESOLVED for the installed system
hypotheses.evidence: A loaded rail collapses in about 3 ms while the other still exceeds 10 V, giving R-VEE and direct-hazard events. Passive per-rail discharge does not couple the rails.

hypotheses.claim: Outputs are disconnected before active discharge begins
hypotheses.evidence: Same EN_E state, no designed ordering, unequal drive paths; switching data and an installed timing bound are missing.

hypotheses.claim: Trip thresholds inside the window establish the 2.1/2.0/0.5 A maximum
hypotheses.evidence: The limiter trips and opens; it does not regulate. Delivered current grows until switch-off, so the worst-case delivered peak is at least trip_max; trip_max is not an upper bound.

hypotheses.claim: Delivered current including overshoot stays within the contract maximum
hypotheses.evidence: Needs a guaranteed detection-to-switch-off time and a load-side di/dt bound. Margins are 15.03 / 4.44 / 39.14 mA (+12 / -12 / +5), so even a 1 us total response allows at most 4.44 mA/us of growth on -12.

next_inputs: D1: the reference side is refuted and the dead zone is set by the pass-pair conduction threshold on both failed rails (D1-S). A minimum-load bleeder (C2) is rejected by owner decision because the pass pair is also the output disconnect, and a fixed gate pre-bias while enabled (C1) is rejected because no fixed floor fits the CSD18543Q3A threshold window. A threshold-independent correction is the next proposal. Nothing is adopted.
D2: OSC per-rail load current versus voltage during shutdown (or an agreed bound), a numeric definition of 'absent', and device switching data for the disconnect/discharge edge.
D3: a guaranteed detection-to-switch-off time and a load-side di/dt bound, or an explicitly agreed regulating current-limit change; no excess-current budget is adopted.
